page: Amazon Web Services m1.medium is a first-generation general-purpose server instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2651 v2 processor running at 1.8 GHz on the i386 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory and a bundled 410 GB local HDD storage volume. There are no integrated GPUs, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of the m1.medium in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield a score of 1284.79, categorizing its processing capability as weak to poor. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers registering at 7.84 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 6.77 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores of 593.15 and 544.51 respectively reflect its legacy hardware profile.

Due to its legacy i386 architecture, lack of modern instruction sets like AVX or AVX-512, and low processing throughput, this instance is not suitable for modern compute-intensive or high-throughput workloads. However, it provides a large 410 GB local HDD storage capacity relative to its compute resources. The m1.medium is best suited for legacy applications, basic file hosting, or lightweight, non-critical background tasks that require persistent local storage but minimal CPU and memory performance.
